points: The November print will show whether the September quarter tracked to the higher 2026 outlook that reports suggest Emerson set after the June-ended quarter; that is the first test of the guidance lift.
With 17 upward revisions versus 1 downward in the past 30 days and 90-day revenue estimates up 0.83%, the report will reveal whether analyst optimism is backed by order and backlog momentum.
Consensus already prices an earnings step-up, from FY1 EPS growth of 9.26% to FY2 EPS growth of 10.40%; management’s guidance will show whether the drivers for that acceleration are intact.
The mixed valuation flag — P/E at 0.4x the theme median but PEG at 3.4x the theme median — means the print must confirm above-average growth execution to keep the relative-value case from unraveling.

Peer prints from INTC on Oct. 23, VRT on Oct. 28 and AMD on Nov. 4 should provide a read on data-center power, semiconductor capex and industrial automation demand ahead of EMR’s call, shaping the setup for the following quarter.
FY1 EPS of $6.56 and FY2 EPS of $7.24 set a high bar; the November guidance update will determine if FY2 estimates can move higher or if they stall into year-end.
watch: 30-day analyst revision ratio stays above 10:1 up/down — supports the long
FY2 EPS growth holds or accelerates above 10.40% vs FY1 — supports the long
90-day revenue estimate direction stays positive — supports the long
PEG1 premium to theme median narrows from 3.4x — supports the long
